asymptotic_scale.r_role: prime order of the declared target subgroup

p_relation.enforcement: accept only p and r with bit_length(p) = bit_length(r) = n

quantifier.curve_measure: the conditional distribution produced by sampler after every declared rejection rule
quantifier.target_measure: s is uniform in {1,...,r-1} and Q=[s]P

sampler.seed_space: uniform infinite bit stream, domain-separated by family_id, n, and field name

prime_sampling.algorithm: draw odd integers uniformly from [2^(n-1),2^n); accept the first candidate with an independently checkable primality certificate
prime_sampling.distribution: uniform over n-bit primes conditional on acceptance

coefficient_sampling.algorithm: draw a,b independently and uniformly from F_p; reject when 4a^3+27b^2 = 0 mod p
coefficient_sampling.distribution: uniform over nonsingular short-Weierstrass coefficient pairs conditional on later family rejections

point_count.algorithm: compute #E(F_p) with a deterministic or certificate-producing point-count algorithm
point_count.independent_verification: a separately implemented verifier checks the certificate and Hasse bound

subgroup_selection.algorithm: accept only #E(F_p)=r with r prime, so the declared subgroup is E(F_p) and the cofactor is one
subgroup_selection.certificate: primality certificate for r and equality certificate r=#E(F_p)
subgroup_selection.independent_verification: verify both certificates and reject bit_length(r) != n

generator_sampling.algorithm: draw x uniformly from F_p until x^3+ax+b is a nonzero quadratic residue; choose either square root with one fair sign bit; set P=(x,y)
generator_sampling.distribution: uniform over E(F_p) minus the identity because r is an odd prime and no affine point has y=0

target_sampling.algorithm: draw s uniformly from {1,...,r-1}; compute Q=[s]P; reveal only p,a,b,r,P,Q and declared certificates to the ECDLP algorithm
target_sampling.distribution: uniform nonidentity target in the subgroup for each sampled generator

rejection_rules.predicate: #E(F_p) is not prime or bit_length(#E(F_p)) != n
rejection_rules.reason: baseline family uses a prime-order full group and equal p/r bit length
trace-one curves admit known polynomial-time attacks and are an exception control
pairing transfers make this a structurally exceptional control

rejection_rules.predicate: p^j = 1 mod r for some 1 <= j <= floor(n^2/max(1,(log2 n)^3))
rejection_rules.reason: exclude a conservative source-scale range in which an L[1/3] finite-field destination is 2^o(n)
separate the two immediately visible extra-automorphism families from the baseline

sampler.failure_semantics: a seed that does not produce an accepted instance within a protocol-fixed draw budget is a retained sampler failure, not evidence about ECDLP hardness

embedding_degree_guard.admission_test: certify p^j != 1 mod r for every integer 1<=j<=K(n); an exact k is not required
embedding_degree_guard.interpretation: this is an exception filter against the named pairing-plus-L[1/3] route, not a hardness certificate or a lower bound for all transfer algorithms

exception_controls.purpose: the classifier must retain a trace-one curve as a known-weak positive control
the classifier must detect a pairing-transfer exception
the source-scale embedding-degree guard must reject a verified small-k curve
the prime-order admission rule must reject a Pohlig-Hellman control
the immediately visible j=0 or j=1728 family must remain a separate stratum
at least one independently certified ordinary prime-order curve must pass every filter
changing one bound identity field must invalidate the certificate or change its digest

algorithm_model.operation_cost_model: probabilistic multi-tape Turing machine bit operations, with field/group/oracle counts retained as secondary units

cost_accounting.parallelism: processors and total work both reported
cost_accounting.success_repetitions: charged to reach declared success probability
cost_accounting.memory: peak live bits and allocation boundary reported
cost_accounting.stored_data: persistent advice/tables in bits reported separately
cost_accounting.communication: messages and transmitted bits reported for parallel/distributed algorithms

success_criterion.correctness_check: verify Q = [s]P in the declared subgroup
success_criterion.expected_time_condition: expectation uses the probability order declared by quantifier.probability_order

claim_boundary.schema_conformance_means: required family, quantifier, model, cost, and control metadata are present
claim_boundary.schema_conformance_does_not_mean: the curve arithmetic, certificates, sampler distribution, hardness, or asymptotic claim is mathematically verified
claim_boundary.experiment_limit: finite experiments can falsify named instruments, heuristics, cost models, or architectures only
claim_boundary.nonexistence_limit: nonexistence requires a proof covering the explicitly stated computation model and family quantifiers
